equity_bridge.item: Deferred and contingent consideration (on and off balance sheet), 30 June 2026
equity_bridge.note: H1 2026 net debt table p.17. A fixed claim for acquisitions already completed whose revenue is in base_revenue; Bunzl itself includes it in 'adjusted net debt'.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_8yr_cagr (FY2017-FY2025, 4.1% in GBP) cross-checked against the base path's FY2026-30 average; equity CAGR is distorted by GBP570m of FY2024-25 buybacks and EPS by the FY2025 North America margin collapse, so neither is a usable growth anchor
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 7.8% vs EPS 5yr CAGR 1.9% and revenue 5yr CAGR 3.2% (>30% divergence): equity growth is retained earnings plus FX reserve moves, not earnings power. 3yr figures are all near zero or negative because GBP strengthened and FY2025 was a profit-warning year.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are on the OWNER series (reported OCF-minus-capex less SBC less lease principal and interest), FY2019 onward only: FY2019 467.3, FY2020 582.6, FY2021 528.8, FY2022 715.7, FY2023 642.3, FY2024 622.6, FY2025 597.5. FY2017-18 are pre-IFRS-16 and not comparable. Owner-FCF 5yr CAGR 0.5% vs reported 2.1%: lease payments have grown from 1.6% to 2.0% of revenue (warehouse consolidation, automation, inflation-linked rent), absorbing an increasing share of reported cash flow. Acquisition spend is NOT deducted from the historical series; it is charged in the forward build.

scenario_narratives.base: North America Distribution's operating-model repair holds (service levels 'largely restored', five consecutive quarters of positive underlying growth) and the group operating margin walks back from 7.6% to ~8.0% by FY2030, not to the FY2024 peak. Bolt-on spend returns to its FY2021-25 cash average of ~3% of revenue and buys ~3.5% acquired growth on top of ~1.5% organic, with the acquired businesses earning the group margin so M&A is roughly value-neutral at a 7.5% GBP WACC. Leases stay at 2% of revenue and the GBP500m buyback is funded from owner FCF without changing per-share value.
scenario_narratives.bull: The turnaround compounds: North America keeps the H1 2026 8% underlying pace into FY2027, own-brand mix and EPR/PFAS compliance work lift the margin through the 8.3% FY2024 peak to ~8.6%, and the >1,300-target pipeline converts at the five-year COMMITTED average of ~GBP450m/yr with 10-11% EBITA-margin bolt-ons mixing up group returns. Terminal cap 20x and 3% terminal growth reflect a compounder the market has historically paid 20x+ FCF for.
scenario_narratives.bear: The 'major change programme execution' risk the board added in FY2025 recurs, or a foodservice/convenience-store downturn hits the 53% North American revenue base again: operating margin falls to ~7.0% in FY2027 and settles at 7.2%, organic growth is ~0.5%, and macro uncertainty keeps acquisition spend at the FY2025 trough for two more years. Lease cost creeps to 2.1% of revenue. With thin margins and no re-rating, the terminal cap is 15x and terminal growth 2%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value the existing distribution business on owner FCF after the full IFRS-16 lease payment, and give credit for bolt-on M&A only to the extent the cash it costs is charged in the same year. Bunzl's economics are a ~7.7% lease-adjusted EBIT margin on a low-growth, low-beta, cash-generative base; the compounding record (c.9% EPS CAGR since 2004) is mostly purchased growth at ~8x EBITA, which is value-accretive but not free. The terminal value is capped at 18x owner FCF so the valuation does not depend on perpetuity arithmetic at a 5pp WACC-minus-g spread.
key_risks_to_valuation: Acquisition economics: the model credits acquired revenue at ~0.85x EV/revenue earning the group margin; if bolt-ons genuinely sustain 13%+ year-2 ROIC the base case understates value, and if the pipeline dries up (2025-style) the growth path is too high.
North America (53% of revenue) margin: a second execution failure would push the group toward the bear path; the base assumes recovery only to the FY2023 level, not the FY2024 peak.
FX translation: ~75% of profit is earned in USD, EUR, CAD, AUD and BRL; a 5% move in GBP shifts GBP flows and the GBP-denominated value by a similar amount with no change in underlying trading.
Lease cost creep: lease payments have risen from 1.6% to 2.0% of revenue since FY2023; each 0.1pp is ~GBP12m/yr of owner FCF.
Terminal cap: the 18x cap binds in every scenario, so the value is essentially 'year-10 owner FCF x 18' discounted; the WACC x g grid moves value less than a change in the cap would.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 1981.0-2898.0 GBp
data_sources.financials: BNZL.L_Metrics.csv (core_metrics, GBP millions, FY2017-FY2025 and H1 FY2026), kpis table (lease principal/interest, D&A, cash taxes, buybacks, diluted shares), FY2025 annual report (cash flow statement lines 8216-8249), H1 2026 interim report (cash flow summary p.17, net debt table, note 7 share count)
data_sources.qualitative: BNZL.L_Analysis.json (2026-10-10); FY2025 annual report outlook; H1 2026 results (1 Sep 2026) guidance and GBP500m buyback

inputs.share_count_basis: Diluted weighted average, six months to 30 June 2026 (H1 2026 note 7: 321.5m basic + 0.8m dilutive employee share plans). Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows. The GBP500m buyback launched 1 Sep 2026 (~12 months) is value-neutral in this model and is not pulled forward into the count.
inputs.net_debt_basis: Bunzl's own 'net debt excluding lease liabilities' at 30 June 2026 (H1 2026 p.17): GBP1,432.3m. total_debt is derived as net debt + cash and includes overdrafts and the fair value of debt-related FX hedges, so it differs slightly from the gross borrowings line. Lease liabilities (GBP740.8m) are EXCLUDED because lease cash is charged in the flows (treatment B). Deferred and contingent consideration (GBP250.5m on and off balance sheet) is deducted in equity_bridge.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 annual report cash-flow reconciliation (note 30): share based payments GBP3.5m, which is net of a one-off GBP7.8m credit disclosed on p.1776; normalised charge GBP11.3m used. Equity-award cash taxes nil (UK net-settlement not used; employee trust purchases are the funding mechanism and are treated as buybacks). H1 2026 charge GBP7.5m.
inputs.interest_income_note: Interest received (GBP50.9m FY2025) sits in investing activities, outside the OCF 913.0 that reported_fcf is built from, so there is nothing to strip. Bunzl is a net borrower; gross cash and gross debt are both netted in the bridge.
inputs.lease_payments_note: FY2025 lease principal GBP192.1m + lease interest GBP40.6m (cash flow statement, financing). Deducted from reported_fcf to reach last_fcf: 841.5 - 11.3 - 232.7 = 597.5.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 financing outflow: purchase of own shares GBP204.8m + employee trust shares GBP46.3m. FY2024: GBP322.9m. H1 2026: nil (programme paused after April 2025 warning; new GBP500m programme announced 1 Sep 2026).

acquisition_cash_history.note: Purchase of businesses net of cash acquired, investing activities. FY2021-25 average GBP354.5m = 3.0% of revenue; this is the anchor for the acquisition-spend component of capex_pct_path.

inputs.fx_note: Statements and flows in GBP millions; LSE quote in pence (GBp = 1/100 GBP). fx_rate 100 converts model GBP per share to the quoted pence. No cross-listing to parity-check; the factor is definitional, not a market rate.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-09T15:35:03Z (LSE regular-session close; not an after-hours print)
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in GBP, the currency of the flows: 10-year gilt ~4.5% (Oct 2026), equity risk premium 5.0%, beta 0.70 (Bunzl is a low-beta defensive distributor; 5-year betas sit 0.6-0.8) gives cost of equity ~8.0%. Pre-tax cost of debt ~5% (FY2026 adjusted net finance expense guided GBP125-130m on ~GBP1.9bn average adjusted net debt), 3.7% after tax at 26%. Weights 84% equity (market cap ~GBP8.8bn) / 16% debt (adjusted net debt GBP1.7bn). WACC = 0.84 x 8.0 + 0.16 x 3.7 = 7.3%, rounded to 7.5% and used in all three scenarios so that cyclicality and execution risk are charged once, in the flows. Translation exposure (53% North America, ~75% of profit in non-GBP currencies) is left in the GBP flows, not in the rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost: the full IFRS-16 lease payment (principal + interest, 2.0% of revenue at FY2025: 232.7 / 11,845.4 = 1.96%; H1 2026 2.01%) is charged inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path, and lease liabilities (GBP740.8m) are EXCLUDED from net debt. ebitda_margin_path is therefore the PRE-lease, pre-SBC adjusted EBITDA (FY2025: adjusted operating profit 902.5 ex the SBC credit + depreciation and software amortisation 253.2 + normalised SBC 11.3 = 1,167.0 = 9.85% of revenue). da_pct_path is depreciation and software amortisation EX right-of-use depreciation and EX acquired-intangibles amortisation (253.2 - 197.8 = 55.4 = 0.47% of revenue), so the lease is not charged twice. Cross-check: 1,167.0 - 11.3 - 232.7 - 55.4 = 867.6 vs Bunzl's own 'lease adjusted operating profit' 875.4 (difference is the SBC credit normalisation).
inputs.nci_treatment: Immaterial: the only NCI is 25% of Nisbets Australia/NZ (GBP2.7m at acquisition, GBP0.6m/yr profit share). Not deducted; noted here so the omission is deliberate.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing row: non-US operating company, with the adaptations file applied for GBP WACC, treatment-B leases, the pence quote and SBC-near-zero). Bunzl is a serial bolt-on acquirer (237 deals since 2004, GBP6.2bn committed), so the single most consequential judgment is how to treat M&A. DECISION: acquisitions are charged as a capex-like line (capex_pct_path = PP&E capex ~0.55% of revenue + acquisition spend), and the revenue growth path credits the growth that spend buys at ~0.85x EV/revenue (Bunzl's disclosed ~8x EV/EBITA on ~10-11% EBITA-margin bolt-ons). Each year's acquisition spend is derived from that year's growth path (acquired growth = spend / 0.85) so the two cannot drift apart, and both fade together into the terminal year. In the base case this makes M&A roughly NPV-neutral (acquired revenue earns the group's 7.7% lease-adjusted EBIT margin, a ~7% post-tax cash yield vs 7.5% WACC) so value comes from the existing business; the bull case lets the acquired margin mix show through. Working capital: Bunzl is a distributor with receivables + inventory > payables (working capital 10.9% of revenue at FY2025), so wc_capture is NEGATIVE, but applied only at ~-3.5% to -4% because the working capital of acquired businesses comes inside the purchase price and only organic growth consumes incremental cash. Cash tax: FY2025 cash tax paid 179.7 on a lease-adjusted EBIT of 875 is 20.5%, but that is a LEVERED cash figure; adding back the ~GBP33m interest tax shield gives ~24.3% unlevered against a 26% guided ETR. Base path 24.5% rising to 25.0% (continued deductibility of acquired goodwill/intangibles in US asset deals). Terminal cap multiple 18x base / 20x bull / 15x bear on a 1.5-2.5% organic-growth distributor; the cap binds in all scenarios. SBC-near-zero market: SBC is ~0.1% of revenue so the house/street band is a few pence wide; band_position will read as degenerate and should be treated as n/a. Buybacks are value-neutral here (SBC expensed, count flat). The current FX translation headwind (GBP strength vs USD/BRL/CAD in 2025) is left to wash through the GBP growth path.

bear.growth_rationale: FY2026 2.0% (H2 slows as the H1 plastic-inflation benefit fades and GBP strength bites). FY2027 1.5%: a second North America execution wobble or a foodservice/convenience downturn takes organic to ~0.5%; acquisition spend stays at the FY2025 trough (~1% of revenue) for two years, then ~2%.
bear.ebitda_margin_rationale: Operating margin slips to ~7.0% in FY2027 (the FY2025 H2 trough rerun: price competition in commoditised categories, cost inflation not passed through) and settles at ~7.2%, below the FY2025 level; the FY2024 8.3% is never regained.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 3.0%: H1 2026 reported +3.0% (constant FX +2.9%, underlying +3.2%), guidance 'moderate growth', FX ~neutral, acquisitions light (H1 GBP26m). FY2027-29 5.0% = organic 1.5% + ~3.5% acquired from spend returning to the FY2021-25 average of 3.0% of revenue. Fades as acquisition spend fades: by FY2035 1.5% organic + 1.5% acquired.
base.ebitda_margin_rationale: Pre-lease, pre-SBC adjusted EBITDA. FY2025 9.85% (operating margin 7.6% underlying), FY2024 10.44% (8.3%), FY2023 9.89% (8.0%). FY2026 held flat at 9.85% per guidance 'operating margin broadly flat' and management's warning that H1's expansion to 7.3% was partly temporary inflation. Then recovers 0.1pp/yr to 10.3% (operating margin ~8.0%, the FY2023 level) as North America Distribution service levels normalise; does NOT assume the FY2024 peak returns.
base.capex_rationale: PP&E and software capex 0.55% of revenue (FY2025 0.60%, FY2024 0.46%, 5yr avg ~0.45%) PLUS acquisition spend = (growth - 1.5% organic) x 0.85: FY2026 1.3% (~GBP160m, 'ahead of FY2025's GBP132m'), FY2027-29 3.0% (the FY2021-25 cash average), fading to 1.3% by FY2035.

bull.growth_rationale: Organic 2.5% (North America wallet-share recovery holds at the H1 2026 8% underlying pace into FY2027, own-brand and EPR/PFAS compliance tailwinds) plus acquired growth from spend of 3.4% of revenue FY2027-29 (~GBP450m, the five-year COMMITTED average), fading to 1.5% acquired by FY2035.
bull.ebitda_margin_rationale: Operating margin recovers through the FY2024 8.3% peak to ~8.6% by FY2030 as higher-margin bolt-ons (10-11% EBITA) mix in and warehouse automation lands.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 18x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the 15/50/35 house default to 25/50/25. Bear up: the April 2025 profit warning showed how a single operating company can swing group results, management has itself flagged H1 2026 margin expansion as partly temporary, and organic growth has been low-single-digit or negative in several recent years. Bull down: it needs two things to go right at once (North America margin recovery past the FY2024 peak AND M&A re-accelerating to ~GBP450m/yr) and the shares have already re-rated 38% off the 1,981p low.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
